-118.44700,34.06480.name: UCLA Fertility Center
-118.44700,34.06480.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Kathleen M. Brennan, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

8.85968,49.10609.name: Charles River Laboratories, Research Models and Services - Germany GmbH
8.85968,49.10609.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

0.51842,51.61134.name: Bourn Hall Clinic Wickford
0.51842,51.61134.state: Bourn Hall Clinic Wickford, 25 London Road, Wickford, Essex, SS12 0AW
0.51842,51.61134.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-67.08236,45.08078.name: St. Andrews Biological Station
-67.08236,45.08078.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, January 2024
-67.08236,45.08078.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. A site of Fisheries and Oceans Canada. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, January 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-81.78000,24.55510.name: Oxitec — US releases and EPA experimental use permits
-81.78000,24.55510.desc: The US permits under which engineered mosquitoes were released in Florida and Texas, with the EPA rather than a biosafety agency as the regulator. An engineered insect is handled as a pesticide in the United States, which determines what review it receives.

77.34110,11.10850.name: Rasi Seeds
77.34110,11.10850.desc: One of the Indian hybrid seed companies holding sub-licences to engineered cotton traits, with a portfolio across cotton, maize, paddy, millet, sunflower and vegetables and a national dealer network. Its presence matters to the shape of this facet rather than to any single event: engineered cotton reached millions of Indian smallholders through a dozen or so domestic hybrid companies like this one, not through the trait owner's own brand. The trait travelled on somebody else's seed, which is why a dispute over royalties between two companies became a national price-control question.
